title: Aitaroun: a border town, before and after
summary: Since 1 March 2026: 795 buildings seen destroyed, as the Village Studio maps them, and 5 fires.

steps.title: A border town
text: Aitaroun sits two kilometres from the Blue Line in the district of Bint Jbeil. Its village damage report reads the town and the ground within 1.5 km of its houses on sharp satellite pictures, and the Village Studio keeps every change it found as a map.
This investigation follows the war of 2026: each change appears on the day it was first seen on a picture, from 1 March 2026.

steps.title: March 2026
text: By the end of March, 5 buildings had been seen destroyed on a dated picture.
steps.note: A change appears on the day it was first seen on a picture, which is when it entered the record, not necessarily when it happened.

steps.title: April 2026
text: By the end of April the count had reached 668: 663 more buildings seen destroyed in one month.

steps.title: What the report has mapped since March
text: Since 1 March 2026 the report has seen 795 buildings destroyed and 50 damaged, and 2.2 km of road cratered or blocked.
It counts 2,516 more destroyed buildings that it cannot date more closely than its own pair of pictures. They are not drawn here, because they cannot be placed after 1 March.

steps.title: Fire round the town
text: 5 fires linked to an Israeli attack are recorded at Aitaroun, from 2 July 2026 to 15 August 2026. Where a burn scar was measured, 4 of them cover 114.0 ha between them.

steps.title: The other records
text: The corpus also holds 2 displacement orders and 2 white phosphorus attacks for Aitaroun, each counted apart.

steps.title: Read it yourself
text: Open the database on Aitaroun to read the town's figures by kind, date and column, and play the timeline over its mapped damage from 1 March 2026. The records themselves are not published; to access them, contact Green Southerners.
